key_insight: FARMS turns computational mathematics into AI-ready knowledge by linking formal statements to source context, algorithmic meaning and quantitative guarantees.
engineering_relevance: Reusable, verifiable mathematical knowledge could help AI systems select and adapt numerical methods for trustworthy computational workflows.
method: Prepare source material and build reusable mathematical representations.
Review semantic fidelity and preserve links to source context.
Use Lean-checked implications from explicit source premises to connect selected statements to computational skills.
evidence_signal: The pipeline accepted 157 of 171 targets in randomized numerical linear algebra and numerical PDEs, with mean estimated costs of US$0.85–2.29 per target across sources; demonstrations included a heat-flow solve and wave-response compression.
watch_item: Lean-checked guarantees cover selected implications under explicit source premises, not end-to-end correctness of arbitrary AI-generated numerical workflows.
paper_title: FARMS: A Verifiable Foundation for Automated Computational Science
